articles.title: Why Premier League faces uncertainty and chaos after Man City ruling
articles.summary: It has taken more than two years, but a judgement finally appears to have been made on the 115 charges levelled against Manchester City. Here's what it means.
body: If you were getting the impression that the saga over Manchester City 's 115 charges was almost over, think again.
Two years and 10 days since the hearing began, and 1,329 days after City were charged, we now know a verdict has been reached, with the club guilty of the majority of financial rule breaches.
BBC Sport was later told the verdict was sent during the week to club executives, who had to sign a non-disclosure agreement to open the file.
A process can appear to be completely watertight, as this one certainly had been, but when the circle of trust is expanded, the chance of information getting out increases.

articles.title: Liverpool sink Everton and end derby drought after Olsson and Kapocs strike
articles.summary: Liverpool beat their local rivals Everton at Anfield in a Women’s Super League fixture for the first time as Beata Olsson’s early header and Cornelia Kapocs’s late finish were enough to end their long run of derby pain.
body: After six wins from six visits to Anfield for Everton in the WSL era and even quips from their former manager Brian Sørensen in previous campaigns about making Anfield their “training pitch” during their persistent run of victories in this showpiece fixture, Liverpool could, at last, enjoy the bragging rights as their fans celebrated in the Kop after a thoroughly deserved 2-0 victory.
The hosts were undeniably the better side and should have scored more goals. Indeed, they would have done had it not been for the heroics of the Everton midfielder Ruby Mace.

When Olsson got in front of her marker, Hannah Blundell, to meet Natalia Ramos’s right-sided corner and angle her header perfectly, diagonally across goal and into the far corner inside the first four minutes, she had scored with such simplicity that you could have been forgiven for thinking Liverpool were set for an easy afternoon. Instead, what followed was something of a slog at times with Liverpool trying to break down an Everton backline that initially proved difficult to open up.

articles.title: Tony Pulis says he and Stoke were ‘cheated’ in 2011 FA Cup final after Manchester City verdict
articles.summary: Manchester City won match 1-0 after goal by Yaya Touré. Club deny wrongdoing and say ‘process is ongoing’ Tony Pulis has said his Stoke City team was “cheated” out of the 2011 FA Cup after Manchester City were found guilty on virtually all counts of breaching Premier League financial rules.
body: Pulis’ Stoke lost the 2011 Cup final 1-0 after Yaya Touré’s strike. Yet following Friday’s news that City are guilty on all but one of the more than 100 charges laid by the Premier League in February 2023, Pulis feels serious discontent. City are expected to appeal and they deny any wrongdoing.

“When do we get our FA Cup?” the 68-year-old wrote in his BBC Sport column. “That is what all Stoke fans have been asking me since the news broke on Friday. I thought exactly the same. I don’t expect Manchester City to offer back the 2011 FA Cup and the winners’ medals their players received. I don’t seriously believe any other trophies and titles will be handed back over either. A points deduction and a massive fine feels far more likely.

“But I still feel cheated. We won’t ever get that day back and the chance to celebrate around Stoke-on-Trent with the cup and medals we so honestly fought for. After breaking the rules, Manchester City got to do that instead. While the process is far from over because City are expected to appeal, I have to say this verdict and the whole situation has left a very sour taste in my mouth.”

articles.title: Parsons becomes record try scorer as Ireland beat Japan
articles.summary: Beibhinn Parsons becomes Ireland women's all-time record try scorer as they hold off a late comeback from Japan to register a 31-24 win in the WXV Global Series at Dexcom Stadium.
body: Tries from Brittany Hogan and Parsons gave the home side the lead after a dominant first half.
Japan looked strong after the restart before Parsons registered her 24th Test try to take the scoring record and help them secure the win.
Scott Bemand will be happy with his side's response after they let a 19-point lead slip away against the USA in their WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium.

Both sides had to navigate a strong wind in Galway, and it was Ireland who adjusted to the challenging conditions the quickest with Hogan showing great persistence to cross from close range after 10 minutes.

articles.title: Czechs beat Ukraine for 12th Billie Jean King Cup title
articles.summary: The Czech Republic ease past Ukraine to win the Billie Jean King Cup for the 12th time thanks to wins for 2026 Wimbledon finalists Karolina Muchova and Linda Noskova.
body: Czech Republic eased past Ukraine to win the Billie Jean King Cup for the 12th time.
This year's Wimbledon finalists Linda Noskova and Karolina Muchova breezed past their opponents to secure a 2-0 victory and deny the Ukrainians a first title in the competition.

Muchova, the runner-up at Wimbledon, comfortably beat Anhelina Kalinina 6-2 6-3 in the opening singles match before Noskova's 6-3 ⁠7-6 (7-5) win over world number seven Elina Svitolina ‌secured the title.
It is the Czechs' first win at the event since 2018, making them the second-most successful nation in its history after the United States, who have 18 titles.

articles.title: Dante Moore injury update: Major concussion news after scary USC hit
articles.summary: Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore suffered a concussion in Saturday’s 41-27 win at USC, and the Ducks’ Heisman Trophy hopeful is expected to return this season after a late hit sent him to a Los Angeles hospital.
body: Moore didn’t suffer any other injuries beyond the concussion, according to a Sunday report from college football reporters Chris Hummer and Matt Zenitz. He’ll now go through concussion protocol, and there’s no immediate timeline for his return.

Moore scrambled in the second quarter at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. He reached the first-down marker and slid. USC linebacker Desman Stephens II hit him late, and the back of Moore’s head slammed into the turf.
Officials ejected Stephens for targeting. Players from both teams came together after the play, and officials flagged both sides for personal fouls.

The game stopped for 15 minutes while trainers treated Moore on the field. The Detroit native was placed on a backboard, loaded onto a cart and driven to an ambulance that took him to Los Angeles General Medical Center. He moved his arms as he left the field.

articles.title: Why latest defeat feels different for Wales
articles.summary: Wales may have suffered another Test defeat, but Sean Lynn's new-look side has given fans plenty to be optimistic about before next month's trip to Japan.
body: As many of the three thousand-plus fans exited Cardiff Arms Park after the USA claimed a 26-24 victory, I assume we did so with a sense of optimism rather than the doom and gloom that often surrounds Welsh rugby.
What head coach Sean Lynn and his backroom staff have done to this group in just six weeks of pre-season is to be applauded.
Wales have been transformed from a side which whimpered out of a winless World Cup and Six Nations into a competitive 80-minute team and one the nation can truly get behind.

Speaking earlier this month, the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) women's rugby director, Nadine Griffiths, said the WXV series would be the real "litmus test" and a "brilliant opportunity to test our progress".

Quarterback Garrett Nussmeier was listed as the emergency quarterback.

Miami’s inactive players include wide receiver Caleb Douglas and edge rusher Robert Beal, Jr. Douglas had been ruled out of the game with an ankle injury while Beal was ruled out with a hamstring issue. Wright was officially doubtful, and now will not play, due to a stinger and a foot issue. Also inactive are cornerback Marcellas Dial, Jr., guard DJ Campbell, and tackle Chukwuebuka Godrick. Quarterback Brady Cook was listed as the third emergency quarterback.
The emergency quarterback designation allows for the inactive quarterback to dress and enter the game if injuries happen to both of the quarterbacks on the game day roster.

articles.title: Do the Knicks have enough frontcourt depth for title defense? 3 reasons for optimism
articles.summary: New York brought back most of its championship roster, but lost backup center Mitchell Robinson. It's a loss for Knicks fans not just because Robinson is an excellent rotation big, but because he was the longest-tenured member of the team. To leave after a title for the rival Celtics just stings.
body: As great as Robinson is as a rebounder, Drummond gives the Knicks another elite option on the glass. And offensively, he's a different type of player. He doesn't finish above the rim like Robinson can. But Drummond is a quicker decision-maker as a passer, a far superior free-throw shooter at over 60% in consecutive years, and he has even started to shoot spot-up 3-pointers. Drummond made 32 of his 90 shots from 3 last season, which is an incredible development for a player who was once one of the most hackable players in the league, much like Robinson is today.

Nobody is confusing Drummond with Karl-Anthony Towns, but these skills give Knicks head coach Mike Brown some extra options with his backup units. Drummond can screen and roll, spot up in the corner or run handoffs. Robinson was more of a run-and-dunk player.

articles.title: Why Tuchel's critics have been forced to stay quiet despite Spain loss
articles.summary: The narrative before this first post-World Cup international was clear: if England lose, the pressure on Thomas Tuchel could become unbearable.
body: The big name on the big bucks, brought in to win the big games, could not afford to lose to Spain after the tactical disaster of the World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina. The court of public opinion, and the bile of the English media, would combine to make life very difficult for the England boss.

Well, here we are, in the aftermath of a 3-2 loss to the newly-crowned world champions, where England were outclassed on numerous occasions, where the scoreline should have been much one-sided, where for long periods Spain looked far superior to the Three Lions, where after half an hour the visitors should have been four-nil up. That's surely it, then? Auf Wiedersehen, Thomas?

Nope. Strangely, despite all of that, Tuchel's critics have been forced to bite their tongues and bide their time. Why? Because England were true to their DNA, they gave it a real good go; there were a lot of positive signs, and ultimately everyone saw again just how incredibly good Spain are.
It's hard to criticise Tuchel or his players when they were narrowly beaten by a team who have repeatedly proven they are the best by a mile at what they do.
points: The narrative before this first post-World Cup international was clear: if England lose, the pressure on Thomas Tuchel could become unbearable.
